statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail sits at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold. A narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where untested hawkish September repricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: the weekend halt holds tail risk at the low-band floor while an absorbed Hormuz disruption sits beside hawkish September repricing
body:
This assessment is made inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The verified anchor remains Friday's completed session, re-checked against the ^NDX quote page this hour and unchanged: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close, leaving the close about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. That is a downside reversal, but it is a finished session rather than an extending trend, and it cannot continue while the tape is shut. VIX ended at 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend.

The open question is policy pricing rather than price structure. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish, lifting September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 57-59% on CME-based futures pricing, with prediction markets spread wider around that level. The move was short-end led: the 2-year yield rose roughly 9-11 basis points toward 4.32-4.34% while the 10-year added about 4bp. H.15 constant-maturity yields for 27 August still read 2Y 4.20%, 5Y 4.38%, 10Y 4.67% and 30Y 5.19%, so the official series sits below Friday's market levels. A curve that flattens on the policy leg reads as a rate-path adjustment rather than a growth scare.

This hour's research extended the cross-asset and geopolitical check. Crude was re-verified at WTI $83.44 and Brent $88.29 for Friday, extending a weekly loss of roughly 4%. That is notable because the Iran conflict remains active: the US blockade and the Treasury sanctions campaign continue, UKMTO carries a severe risk assessment for the Strait of Hormuz, and US Central Command reports 82 commercial vessels redirected. Oil falling into that backdrop indicates the market is absorbing a persistent, well-known disruption rather than repricing a fresh discontinuity, which keeps the story in Stress rather than Tail. Equities fell while VIX fell, so the cross-asset stack is only partially aligned - the configuration in which mean reversion generally survives.

Tail is therefore held at the low-band floor of 5 with dominant mode normal, because none of the amplifiers the score measures - shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, NQ holding near a session extreme - can exist without a tape. Stress is 26, carrying untested hawkish repricing, month-end flows into Monday and the unresolved Hormuz disruption. Confidence is 78: the price, volatility, rates, oil, policy and calendar evidence was all re-verified against primary sources this hour, offset slightly by the absence of any live price path and by shared cross-asset context that is beyond its freshness window today.

A narrow observation window is flagged from 22:00 to 23:30 UTC for the Sunday futures reopen, where the first live test of near-coin-flip September pricing meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Every post-reopen structure in the forecast is stated conditionally because none of it is observable now.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday midday through this morning. The series was uniformly green with Tail held at 5, dominant mode normal and Stress in a narrow 25-26 band throughout. Confidence decayed from 73 to 58 as the published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76 and 77 on the seven most recent refreshes as primary sources were re-verified. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next ten projected hours fall inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 as the reopen approaches and Confidence decays from 78 to 69 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen tonight Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and well below the block threshold, covering the first live test of near-coin-flip September rate pricing, thin reopen liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases through 11, 10 and 9 across the Asian session to 8 into the European morning on expected volatility decay, ticking back to 9 around the European cash open, while Confidence recovers to 73 because a live tape would exist again. Every post-reopen structure is stated conditionally; the stated invalidations are repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near a session extreme. Monday 31 August brings month-end flows and a UK bank holiday that would conditionally thin the European handover, with Dallas Fed Manufacturing at 14:30 UTC the only scheduled US release that day and outside this horizon. The data-heavy week beyond the horizon opens with ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September and runs to August payrolls on 4 September.
